diagrams.title: First-County Lien Entry Workflow
diagrams.subtitle: From a phone call to the county to a logged certificate

stages.label: Call the County
stages.detail: Ask how many liens sold last year and how many people attended; 200 to 500 liens with 20 bidders beats 30 liens with 50.

stages.label: Learn the State Ceiling
stages.detail: Statutory ceilings cited include Florida 18%, Arizona 16%, Iowa 24% and Illinois 36%.

stages.label: Look at the Parcel and Set an Exit
stages.detail: No bid on any parcel you have not looked at and have no exit strategy for; never bid on a lien you would not be comfortable owning.

stages.label: Bid Above Zero in Florida
stages.detail: A $1,000 lien bid at 0.25% and redeemed in 3 months pays the 5% floor of $50; a 0% bid gets no minimum at all.

stages.label: Log Dates and Reserve Legal Fees
stages.detail: Record redemption and expiration dates the day you buy (Florida certificates expire without a deed application within seven years) and reserve roughly $2,000 to $5,000 per file for attorney and foreclosure fees.

diagrams.caption: Start small in one county: size the competition, know the rate ceiling, look before bidding, respect the Florida floor, and calendar every deadline.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Rates and redemption floors are state-specific practitioner claims; the five-step order is an organizing sequence built from their separate tips.
diagrams.note: Sources: Dustin Hahn (eNKIUQC6io0 @ 00:05:44); Ted Thomas via Gerald Harris (nMj50Itu21Q @ 00:03:13); Ted Thomas (JcAwqIfK0vo @ 00:12:26); Lien Ledger (H9fPhqUYPfc @ 00:04:40, 00:05:50, 00:08:00); Tax Sale Secrets (fIPCLCdZlAU @ 00:08:59).

diagrams.title: Over-the-Counter Leftover List Funnel
diagrams.subtitle: How a full county leftover list narrows to a first purchase

stages.label: Full Leftover List Screened
stages.detail: Parcels that drew no winning bid, sold by the treasurer for back taxes under names like scavenger, strike off, or lands available.

stages.label: Decent After Desk Screen
stages.detail: Desk diligence on county records, tax records, maps, Google Maps, and sold and for-sale comps; site visits skipped on deeds under $1,000.

stages.label: Great Parcels Identified
stages.detail: Most of the list is crap, but a handful are worth buying.

stages.label: Utility, Access and Title Gate
stages.detail: Confirm power, sewer and access (a $1,500 lot needed $20,000 to bring power), match by parcel ID, and screen for IRS liens and buried gas tanks.

stages.label: First-Buy Cap
stages.detail: Cap first buys at one or two liens and one deed and sell before buying more, after a student stacked 40 unsold properties.

diagrams.caption: The leftover list is a screening exercise: roughly one in ten parcels is decent and a handful are great, and first buys stay capped until one sells.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The 1,000-to-100-to-5 yield is the Tax Sale Support hosts' estimate; the purchase cap is Ted Thomas's rule. John Lane and Tax Deed Wolf counter that most leftovers carry major problems or are overpriced.
diagrams.note: Sources: Tax Sale Support (5t3VbtPlElc @ 00:39:46, 00:50:20); Dustin Hahn (uiH28IFKgC4 @ 00:03:46, 00:04:31; YVYW5E5cTUI @ 00:03:22); Saen Higgins (nbHUraglUQo @ 00:07:11); Ted Thomas (XLUuBoGUOj8 @ 00:09:47).

diagrams.title: Cook County Redemption Waterfall
diagrams.subtitle: Overall redemption versus Chicago's south and west sides

bars.label: Redeemed on South and West Sides

diagrams.caption: Countywide, almost every Cook County lien pays off; in rougher Chicago neighborhoods the odds of ending up owning the parcel rise sharply.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Unredeemed shares are the arithmetic complement of Bob Diamond's 96% and about-70% redemption figures; Illinois rules, including the 22-5 notice deadline of four months and 15 days, decide whether a lien holds.

diagrams.title: Lien Versus Deed Odds and Returns
diagrams.subtitle: Redemption odds, interest, penalties and discounts by model

bars.label: Tax Deed Auction Discount
bars.display: 10 to 20 cents on the dollar (60% to 80% off)

diagrams.caption: Lien buyers price for yield because nearly all liens redeem; deed buyers price for discount because ownership is the likely outcome.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Ranges are practitioner estimates; the 'typical' lien interest marker uses Ted Thomas's 18% example, and the deed discount midpoint uses his 70% example.
diagrams.note: Sources: Dustin Hahn (wemMjCnrX34 @ 00:01:09); Tax Sale Secrets (0adTzNpuLtk @ 00:11:13); Ted Thomas (x3XX9ysKcUA @ 00:04:16; jWaS4Y2Z1Mg @ 00:02:24); Cecil Jones (Yq9tyhYQJGY @ 00:03:41).

diagrams.title: Online Auction Bid Gates
diagrams.subtitle: Four checks before a parcel earns a bid

nodes.question: Is there a current photo or boots on the ground?
nodes.fail_action: No bid; county and Street View shots run years stale.

nodes.question: Does the property appraiser site confirm usage and description?
nodes.fail_action: Drop it; never rely on the vendor's assessed value or listing photo, and eliminate landlocked parcels.

nodes.question: Is title clear of hidden, municipal and IRS liens, plus any surviving deed of trust on Texas redemption deeds?
nodes.fail_action: Pass, or price the encumbrance before going further.

nodes.question: Is the exit chosen (quiet title or as-is wholesale) and a CMA-based maximum written down?
nodes.pass_next: Bid up to the written maximum and stay emotionally uninvolved.
nodes.fail_action: Hold off until the exit and ceiling are fixed.

diagrams.caption: Cheap online deeds still demand a current image, appraiser-site verification, a title search and a fixed exit before any bid.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Practitioners disagree on buying sight-unseen; these gates follow the stricter view. Tax Sale Secrets reports losing seven or eight Florida properties before winning one under disciplined maximums.
diagrams.note: Sources: Tax Sale Secrets (IMGzMnzQiZQ @ 01:29:27; RgLErVu5_Kk @ 00:29:54, 00:48:38; AO4ZqaMio7s @ 00:27:24); The Jackie Jackson | Tax Deed & Real Estate Coach (Pz2ZCMuIox4 @ 00:12:04); Ted Thomas (41UuQtBLiBo @ 00:03:04).

diagrams.title: Post-Tyler Certificate Control Structure
diagrams.subtitle: Who guards a certificate after Tyler v. Hennepin

center.headcount: Solo holder backed by tax sale counsel
center.focus: Protect each certificate from notice defects, bankruptcy stays, equity claims and unconfirmed redemptions.

spokes.kpi: Confirms how the county issues deeds; mandamus or judicial foreclosure plus suing the county as the fallback.
Court file and county records pulled on every certificate; ready for the court form's question on equity in the property.
Every interest holder noticed, including trustees, with additional reasonable steps documented after certified mail comes back.
Bankruptcy checked up to the minute of sale (a 9:48 a.m. filing voids a 10:00 a.m. auction); ticklers at two and three weeks after a redemption closing until proof arrives.

diagrams.caption: After the 9-0 Tyler ruling, a certificate is only as safe as its notice trail, its bankruptcy check and written proof of redemption.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Roles are functions, not required hires. Practitioners split sharply: Lynette Lowitz would not buy certificates now, while Tax Sale Secrets frames the worst case as a few months of delay.
diagrams.note: Sources: Tax Sale Resources (d67aVfAEUxg @ 00:25:05); The Devine Law Group (qAoyeFTuxms @ 00:15:05, 00:16:45); Florida Trust, Real Estate, Probate, & Foreclosure (RlQwxNYiqok @ 00:15:33); Behind The Servicing (au90-c2Pwvo @ 00:00:17); The Deed | Real Estate (sb6T0Xe5siY @ 00:06:20).

diagrams.title: Auction Format Yield Bands
diagrams.subtitle: The statutory rate is a ceiling; the format decides the real yield
diagrams.total_range: 0% to 18% depending on state and auction format

buckets.label: Florida Interest Bid-Down
buckets.notes: Quarter-point bids still collect the 5% penalty on fast redemption, but a quarter-point lien held two years yields only about 2.5% a year.

buckets.label: Arizona Proxy Bidding
buckets.notes: A lone 5% bid clears at the 16% maximum in proxy counties; in direct bid counties the same bid locks in 5%.

buckets.label: Colorado Premium Bidding
buckets.notes: About 13% in 2026, set at 9% over the federal discount rate, with a 3-year redemption period; confirm overbid treatment first.

buckets.label: New Jersey Bid-Down to Premium
buckets.notes: Bids run 18% to 0%, then flip into dollar premiums; large investors scoop up sales at 0%.

diagrams.caption: Institutional money grinds popular counties toward zero, yet floors, proxy engines and fixed premium rates still leave pockets of real yield.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Yields assume redemption on the stated terms; operators split on whether quarter-point fast-five plays are smart bets or traps when liens sit unredeemed for years.
diagrams.note: Sources: Tax Sale Resources (XbThUArmcIE @ 00:01:24, 00:02:11); Realauction (cleRXY7vybQ @ 00:02:20; hKsLdKqVOE0 @ 00:01:12); Tax Sale Secrets (stFlmSmpP3Q @ 00:01:09); Tax Lien School Highlights - Dustin Hahn (mHvzzGVcYdI @ 00:01:53); Tax Sale Academy (0I_mhnrF0So @ 00:02:42).

diagrams.title: Four-Week Funding and Scaling Roadmap
diagrams.subtitle: Bankroll, entity, exit and calendar before sale season

weeks.title: Set the Bankroll and Start Transfers
weeks.deliverable: At least $20,000 to $25,000 earmarked; custodian transfers started, since moves out of Equity Trust take two to three weeks.
weeks.gate: No sale-season bidding on $500; funds in motion before Illinois sales open in October.

weeks.title: Stand Up the Bidding Entity
weeks.deliverable: Bids in the IRA's exact name with its own TIN and bank account; one Wyoming lien LLC paired with one LLC per deed.
weeks.gate: Bidding site accepts the entity and its account.

weeks.title: Lock the Exit and REO Offload
weeks.deliverable: Exit strategy fixed before any maximum bid; REO offload channel proven for Georgia and Texas, where REO rates run at least 60%.
weeks.gate: Maximum bid written down with no room for auction fever.

weeks.title: Calendar Notices and Budget Counsel
weeks.deliverable: Every noticing deadline calendared with proof of delivery; $2,000 to $5,000 per property reserved for a tax attorney's clear title action.
weeks.gate: Subsequent-tax payments planned to keep control of each lien.

diagrams.caption: Funding engines run through self-directed retirement money, entity wrappers and other people's money, such as 10% notes funding 20% Georgia redemptions.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The four-week sequence is an organizing frame. Stephen Morel says matching bank-level 15-18% yields takes six to seven figures because institutions absorb roughly 80% of delinquent liens.
diagrams.note: Sources: REtipster with Ted Thomas (jDYlxXpw-e4 @ 00:36:45, 00:41:33); Platinum Investment Properties Group - Tax Liens (AcKbZeNuPr4 @ 00:21:38, 00:50:34); CamaPlan Self Directed IRA (U08uLxrDVE4 @ 00:36:29; DHgFebJCtQU @ 00:18:45); Ross Budrakey (VmzztAnZ71w @ 00:36:42, 01:24:13); Kevin Bupp - Cash Flow Investor (UyiZp8ocowM @ 00:14:17, 00:39:08).
